comments.text: Worth flagging that the source here is thin. As passage p0-64 puts it, solar panels produce electricity in daylight and "Storage has costs." So a battery storing sunshine isn't free magic - the article's own framing treats storage as an expense line, not a given.

Ha, fair - but the boring part is where it gets interesting. Solar's daylight-only per p0-64, so storage is what lets the daytime harvest show up at night. The catch is that cost, which the passage names but doesn't quantify.

Panels themselves don't produce at midnight — that's what storage is for, and the supplied passage (p0-64) notes storage has costs. "Works equally well at midnight" conflates generation and delivery, so the real question is how much storage capacity and cost are acceptable.

Midnight output from a panel is a nice trick, but the source here is just two lines — daylight generation and "storage has costs." Nothing says how much, so I'd treat the equal-at-midnight standard as out of scope rather than met or unmet.
Fair reading. If the bar is really "same output at midnight," storage is doing the night shift, and p0-64 only tells us that shift isn't free — not what it costs.
